newsitem.title: JAPAN: DRAM oversupply to continue til end-98--Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: DRAM oversupply to continue til end-98--Dataquest.

text.p: Market research firm Dataquest said on Monday that oversupply of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips is likely to continue until the end of 1998.
"Until the end of 1998, oversupply of DRAMS...will likely continue," Dataquest senior analyst Masahiro Suzuki told a seminar in Tokyo.
Suzuki added that prices of 16-megabit DRAMS for volume users would likely range between $8 and $9 in calendar 1997, then decline to between $7.50 and $8 in 1998.
He also forecast that prices of 64-megabit DRAMS for volume users would range between $60 and $85 in 1997, then decline to between $35 and $55 in 1998.
Suzuki also said he expected demand for DRAMs to be led by personal computer (PC) makers.
He said production of 64-megabit DRAMS would likely increase gradually until the end of 1998 rather than surging sharply.
